title: Pivot to a host and process pattern
objectives: Select process launches on an exact actor host.
Use a bounded suffix regex with nocase.
Distinguish process presence from execution intent and maliciousness.
story: Signal Desk asks whether an approved host launched a familiar shell. No execution is initiated by the course; you only search authorized telemetry. A process name is a pivot, not a verdict.

teaching.heading: From an identity to an endpoint
teaching.text: An IOC enrichment workflow changes the next question as evidence appears. Here the pivot is an approved host selected privately in SecOps, represented as [HOST] externally. The symbolic task uses principal.hostname as the actor host and target.process.file.full_path as the launched process path. Verify this mapping in your source.

teaching.heading: Regex is a precise pattern
teaching.text: The literal /\\powershell\.exe$/ matches a Windows path ending with a backslash followed by powershell.exe. The escaped dot means a literal period, and $ means the suffix ends there. nocase handles filename case. A suffix does not verify the binary's hash, signer, command line, or intent.

teaching.heading: Know the engine
teaching.text: SecOps documents RE2 regex behavior. Lookahead and lookbehind are not supported. Our app offers predefined patterns only and does not execute regex against data. A supported alternative can split shell names into OR branches or use the documented re.regex function; it must retain the same match semantics.

teaching.heading: Preserve the investigative boundary
teaching.text: Do not run or simulate a suspicious command to generate a match. Use existing authorized process telemetry. If the source stores a different path shape, adapt only inside SecOps and retain the limitation in workplace notes.

challenges.title: Find a PowerShell path suffix
challenges.prompt: Select PROCESS_LAUNCH events on principal.hostname [HOST], with target.process.file.full_path ending in a Windows path suffix \\powershell.exe, case-insensitive. Return event rows.
hints: Keep event category and host scope before selecting a process pattern.
Choose the Windows PowerShell suffix pattern and enable nocase; the end anchor matters.

methodQuestions.prompt: What does this process pattern establish?

options.label: That every PowerShell launch is malicious
That the binary has a trusted signer
That the normalized path matches the specified suffix

methodQuestions.rationale: The pattern checks path text. It is not a hash, signer, execution intent, or compromise test.

methodQuestions.prompt: Which proposed pattern feature needs rejection for RE2?
methodQuestions.rationale: Google documents RE2 without lookahead/lookbehind. Use supported pattern forms.

executeSteps: Choose an approved host in SecOps and inspect the process event's field mapping.
Replace __HOST__ only there, run the query, and inspect available process details.
Do not launch any process to manufacture results.
If Linux paths or another mapping are used, note that this Windows-suffix exercise may be unavailable; complete symbolic mastery independently.
challenges.debrief: Privately list contextual evidence you would need before escalating a shell launch. Never put command lines or process paths from work into the site.

challenges.title: Allow either shell name without broadening scope
challenges.prompt: Select PROCESS_LAUNCH events on [HOST] whose target process path ends with either \\powershell.exe or \\pwsh.exe, case-insensitive. Both alternatives must stay inside the event/host scope.
acceptedVariants:
metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH" AND principal.hostname = "__HOST__" AND
(target.process.file.full_path = /\\powershell\.exe$/ nocase OR target.process.file.full_path = /\\pwsh\.exe$/ nocase)
hints: The two shell names are alternatives; host and event type remain required.
Use the predefined combined suffix pattern or an OR of the two suffix patterns.

methodQuestions.prompt: Why is an unanchored /powershell/ pattern not equivalent?

options.label: It can match unrelated path substrings rather than the exact suffix

methodQuestions.rationale: Anchors and escaping define intent. Looser matches may be useful elsewhere but do not meet this task.

methodQuestions.prompt: No process rows appear. What should you do?

options.label: Conclude the host never launches shells
Check available endpoint telemetry, source mapping, range, and platform applicability
Install an agent on the work device

methodQuestions.rationale: The course requires no installation and cannot establish telemetry coverage. Missing data remains a limitation.

executeSteps: Reuse the authorized host privately and run the two-name query.
Check event details to distinguish path pattern matches from actual activity context.
Compare privately against the single-name filter if telemetry exists.
If unavailable, keep practice pending and continue the symbolic course; do not generate endpoint data.
challenges.debrief: Explain why this expansion is intentional and bounded, whereas dropping the host filter is a different question.
